items.statement: Every OSFP record MUST carry osfpVersion, recordType, and an id that is never reused.
Every timestamp in an OSFP record MUST be a UTC date-time in RFC 3339 format.
A consumer MUST ignore fields it does not recognize, and MUST reject a record whose osfpVersion it does not support.
A consumer MUST NOT treat a status or state value it does not recognize as success.
A producer MUST NOT change an OSFP record after writing it; a change of state is a new record with a new id.
A consumer MUST reject a record that reuses a known id with different content.
A factory MUST record a task grant before it dispatches any attempt of that task.
A factory MUST NOT treat a request, an instruction, a skill, or a tool listing as a grant of authority.
A grant MUST list every resource, operation, and disclosure it permits, and a factory MUST deny any that the grant does not list.
Before each side effect it performs or relays, a factory MUST confirm that the task's latest grant is unexpired and permits that side effect, and MUST NOT perform it otherwise.
For each restriction in a grant, a factory MUST record whether it is enforced or only conveyed to the harness as an instruction, and MUST NOT record an instruction as enforced.
Each disclosure in a grant MUST name its source, its revision, and its destination.
A factory MUST NOT place a credential in a model's input.
A factory SHOULD keep credentials out of reach of code that a model writes, for example behind a proxy outside the harness's sandbox, or as short-lived tokens limited to the grant.
A grant's approvedBy MUST name the person who approved it, or the person who approved the standing grant it derives from.
A grant derived from a standing grant MUST NOT permit anything the standing grant does not permit, and MUST NOT expire later than it.
A factory MUST persist an attempt's identity before it dispatches the attempt to a harness.
An outcome MUST be in exactly one of these states: admitted, started, waiting, completed, failed, canceled, rejected, or unknown.
A factory MUST NOT record started until the harness acknowledges the attempt; admitting an attempt is not starting it.
When a factory cannot establish whether an attempt ran or what it changed, it MUST record the state unknown.
While an attempt is unknown, a factory MUST NOT start another attempt for the same request without a person's decision.
A factory MUST record a stop as three separate facts, each with its own time: stop requested, stop confirmed, and cleanup confirmed.
A factory MUST NOT record cleanup as confirmed until every process, container, and volume the attempt created is gone; the exit of a lead process does not confirm cleanup.
When a factory sends a command to a harness again, it MUST reuse the command's original identity, and MUST NOT reuse that identity for a different command.
Verification evidence MUST be an in-toto Statement whose subject identifies the checked tree by a gitTree or dirHash digest.
Each check in the evidence MUST report exactly one status: passed, failed, not-run, or incomplete.
A check MUST NOT report passed unless it examined at least one unit; a skipped unit is not examined.
A check MUST record the exit status of the command that ran it, not the status of a command that read its output.
If a check's output was cut off, or the tree's digest changed between the check's start and its end, the check MUST report incomplete.
If an attempt changed a test, a grader, an assertion, or any code or configuration that decides a check's result, the evidence MUST say so for that check.
A factory MUST NOT accept text written by a model as verification evidence.
Findings from static analysis SHOULD be recorded in SARIF 2.1.0 and referenced from the evidence by digest.
A factory MUST record each verdict with a reference to the evidence it reviewed, and MUST NOT change the status of any check because of a verdict.
Evidence SHOULD be signed in a DSSE envelope.
A consumer MUST NOT count a check as passed if its evidence says the attempt changed what decides its result or could read its expected answers, unless a person decides it may.
If an attempt could read the expected answers or a reference implementation that a check compares against, the evidence MUST say so for that check.
A grant MUST state, for each attempt, a deadline for the harness to acknowledge the start and a total time budget.
A supervisor MUST run the timer that enforces an attempt's limits outside the loop that runs the attempt.
When a limit expires, a supervisor MUST request a stop of the attempt.
An attempt of a scheduled task MUST send a started event before it does any work.
An attempt of an inspection task that inspected nothing MUST report the result aborted, never clean.
Progress events SHOULD be sent as CloudEvents.
A supervisor SHOULD alert a person only when a decision or a sign-off is needed.
A supervisor MUST report a scheduled task that sent no started event by its expected start as not-run, and one that started but did not finish within its total budget as died.
A factory that runs harnesses through UHP MUST map each UHP task to exactly one OSFP attempt, and MUST keep its own attempt identity after the harness stops retaining the idempotency key.
When a factory reports an outcome over A2A, it MUST map unknown to TASK_STATE_UNSPECIFIED, never to a terminal state.
When a grant provides a tool from an MCP server, the grant MUST identify the tool by the server's name and the tool's name.
Traces of an attempt SHOULD use OpenTelemetry and SHOULD carry the OSFP task and attempt identifiers as attributes.
When a factory reads an A2A task, it MUST treat TASK_STATE_UNSPECIFIED, or a missing state, as unknown.
A factory that reports unknown over A2A in JSON SHOULD emit the state field even though it holds the default value.
